processes.name: Counterparty book-move scripts for Netco separation
processes.description: Gas risk staff send lists of counterparties or books to IT/Cecilia Cheung, who runs a script to move financial deals between books and retranslates. Requirements are clarified by email over several rounds and each new book needs a fresh request.
processes.stall_points: Parameters (which book, commodity, cutoff date, Canadian vs US logic) are clarified by back-and-forth emails before the script runs; the same instructions are re-sent for each new book.
processes.automation: A parameterised book-move request form with the book, commodity and cutoff fields captured once and a status notification when the script completes.

processes.name: Trader and staff system access and environment migration setup (UBSW)
processes.description: IT and desk leads chase each trader or user for how they access Stack Manager, issue production IDs, and circulate curve-file, URL and access-tool changes. Each change is sent by email and users reply individually.
processes.stall_points: Users do not reply to the first survey so a second chaser goes out; curve file and URL changes must be re-communicated by email to each desk.
processes.automation: A tracked checklist or form that records each user's access method and automatically reminds non-responders, plus a single maintained page for curve-file and URL changes.

evidence.quote: If you're receiving this email its because we're still waiting on a response from you.  Please reply to this message ASAP.

processes.name: Daily Energy Market Report and gas/power daily PDF distribution
processes.description: Each trading day an assistant forwards the Energy Market Report to the traders and Theresa Villeggiante sends the Gas Daily and Power Daily PDFs. Distribution lists are maintained by hand and members ask to be added.
processes.stall_points: Distribution list changes are handled by email with a name list requested; when Gas Daily is not loaded yet the sender has to check back and re-send.
processes.automation: An automated scheduled distribution from a maintained list that sends the report when published and tracks list membership.

processes.name: Expense report approvals in Concur/XMS
processes.description: The approver receives an automatic Concur email for each expense report submitted on behalf of team members and approves it via link. Pre-closing expenses are being pushed through before the UBSW transaction.
processes.stall_points: Each report arrives as a separate email needing a manual click-through approval; reports from the same people recur frequently.
processes.automation: Rule-based auto-approval of small reports within policy with a single digest for exceptions.

evidence.quote: The following expense report is ready for approval:
To approve this expense report, click on the following link for Concur Expense.
Note to approvers - please approve these expense reports quickly.

processes.name: Onboarding and HR compliance chasers for UBS transition
processes.description: HR and admins send reminders, forms and attendance requests (drug tests, UBS applications, orientation RSVPs, migration compliance certificates), often per individual, and collect replies by email.
processes.stall_points: The same reminder is sent repeatedly to non-responders and individual records are updated by hand.
processes.automation: A tracker of required onboarding items per person with automatic reminders and RSVP capture.

processes.name: NSS and PGL month-end P&L clean-up and restatement
processes.description: Gas desk and accounting staff reconcile booked deals, annuities and options against contracts after January close, then restate P&L files and circulate the findings by email.
processes.stall_points: Errors in how deals were killed or annuities booked are found after close, requiring reversing entries, restated files and extra calls.
processes.automation: Automated tie-out of booked deal volumes and annuities to contract terms and a restatement diff before close.

processes.name: Estate account exception requests
processes.description: Portland real-time and scheduling managers must identify which UBS staff need extended estate (EST) accounts and request each extension by email to IT with a business reason and duration. Discussion occurs over multiple replies.
processes.stall_points: Decision-makers debate by reply-all chain and the actual request must be written per user.
processes.automation: A single request form with named users, business reason and duration routed to IT approvers.

processes.name: CAISO market notices and real-time schedule checkouts
processes.description: Real-time and scheduling staff receive a steady flow of CAISO notices and reports and perform schedule checkouts with counterparties when the EPE schedule sheet is incomplete.
processes.stall_points: The EPE schedule sheet repeatedly misses tags because counterparties omit the PSE, so schedules are found by manual calls.
processes.automation: Automated reconciliation of tags in the schedule sheet against dispatcher schedules with alerts on missing tags.
